# profile-assign

`updateProfile(user, fields)` applies only `displayName`, `email` and `bio`, in place, atomically: if the body contains any other key the function throws an `Error` before changing anything. Empty bodies are fine.

prompt: Security ticket for the profile endpoint (CWE-915). Problem: `updateProfile` copies every field of the request body onto the user object with `Object.assign`: a body with `isAdmin: true` escalates privileges, and a JSON body with a `__proto__` key replaces the user's prototype so inherited flags such as `isAdmin` appear out of nowhere. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.

start.README.md:
# shell-echo

`archiveLabel(name)` returns exactly `archiving <name>\n`: the tool receives the name as a single argument; `;`, `&&`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, quotes, `*`, newlines and spaces are ordinary characters. No shell may be involved.

prompt: We had an incident review for the archive tool. Root cause: `archiveLabel` builds a shell command line from the archive name (`echo archiving <name>`) and runs it with `exec`: a name such as `x; echo INJECTED` or `$(echo INJECTED)` runs extra commands, and names with quotes or `$` are mangled. Close the hole in `archiveLabel` and anything that shares the flaw in this repository; normal users must notice nothing.

start.README.md:
# query-builder

`findUserQuery(name)` returns `{ text: 'SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE name = $1', values: [name] }` for every name (the name never appears in `text`). `listUsersQuery(column, direction)` only accepts the listed columns and directions (it cannot be parameterised, so it validates) and returns the normalised upper-case direction; anything else throws.

prompt: A penetration test of the user search API reported a vulnerability: `findUserQuery` and `listUsersQuery` paste the search term and the sort column into the SQL text (`WHERE name = '<name>'`, `ORDER BY <column>`), so `' OR '1'='1` returns every user and `name; DROP TABLE users` is a stacked statement waiting for a driver that allows it. Fix it in the code so the whole class of problem is gone (not just the payload from the report) and keep everything legitimate working. README.md describes the intended behaviour.

start.README.md:
# url-allowlist

`isAllowedTarget(url)` parses the URL with the WHATWG `URL` class and compares the parsed parts (protocol `https:`, hostname exactly `hooks.partner.example`, port empty or 443, no username/password). Whatever the parser disagrees with the old string test about is not allowed.

prompt: isAllowedTarget is unsafe: `isAllowedTarget` checks the text of the URL with `startsWith('https://hooks.partner.example')`, so `https://hooks.partner.example.evil.io/`, `https://hooks.partner.example@evil.io/` and `https://hooks.partner.example:8443/` are accepted and the sender posts to hosts nobody approved. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.

start.README.md:
# upload-path

`readUpload(root, name)` keeps working for every name that stays inside `root` (also `sub/../ok.txt`, `a..b.txt`, `..hidden`) and throws for everything that leaves it, including symbolic links inside `root` that point outside (check the real path).

prompt: readUpload is unsafe: `readUpload` joins the requested name onto the upload directory with `path.join`, which happily normalises `../` out of the directory: `GET /files?name=../../etc/passwd` (or an absolute path, or a symlink that was uploaded) reads files anywhere the server can. fix it without breaking normal use, README.md says what normal is.

start.README.md:
# search-regex

`filterItems(items, query)` is a case-insensitive substring search (no regular expressions): `a.c` finds `a.c` but not `abc`, `(` and `[` are harmless, hostile patterns cost nothing.

prompt: Review comment on `filterItems`: `filterItems` turns the search box content into a regular expression: `(` or `[` makes the request throw, `.` and `*` match more than the user typed, and a query like `(a+)+$` against a long item name makes the single-threaded server spin in catastrophic backtracking. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.

start.README.md:
# token-alg

`verifyToken(token, secret)` accepts only tokens whose header `alg` is exactly `HS256` and whose HMAC verifies (compare with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, handling length differences). `none`, other spellings, other algorithms, missing or empty signatures, wrong part counts and bad encodings all throw.

prompt: Our static analysis flagged `verifyToken` (CWE-347): `verifyToken` reads the algorithm from the token header and treats `alg: none` as "nothing to verify": a token with any claims and an empty signature is accepted, and other `alg` values are verified as HS256 without question. Harden the code. Existing behaviour for legitimate callers has to stay exactly as documented in README.md; there are tests for both the normal use and for hostile input.

start.README.md:
# deep-merge

`deepMerge(target, source)` keeps its merge semantics (nested objects merged, arrays/scalars/null replace) and silently skips the keys `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` at every depth; `Object.prototype` is never modified and neither are other prototypes reachable through the target.

prompt: Review comment on `deepMerge`: `deepMerge` recurses into whatever keys the source has: merging a JSON body such as `{"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}}` writes `isAdmin` into `Object.prototype`, so every object in the process suddenly has it (prototype pollution). Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.

start.README.md:
# set-path

`setPath(obj, path, value)` validates the whole path first (TypeError for `__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype` segments, empty paths and empty segments) and only then writes. Creation of objects/arrays and replacement of non-object values on the way work as before; inherited properties are never followed or written.

prompt: Our static analysis flagged `setPath` (CWE-1321): `setPath(obj, 'a.b.c', value)` walks the dotted path from user-chosen form field names (`user.address.city`) and creates what is missing; a field named `__proto__.isAdmin` walks into `Object.prototype` and sets the flag on every object of the process. Harden the code. Existing behaviour for legitimate callers has to stay exactly as documented in README.md; there are tests for both the normal use and for hostile input.

start.README.md:
# slug-regex

`isValidSlug(s)` follows its comment exactly (the old pattern also accepted a trailing hyphen: `abc-` is no longer valid) and runs in linear time for any input, up to megabytes.

prompt: Security ticket for the CMS routes (CWE-1333). Problem: `isValidSlug` uses `/^([a-z0-9]+-?)+$/`: a 40-character slug followed by an invalid character makes the engine try every way of splitting the run of letters, which takes exponential time, and a single request freezes the whole single-threaded server. Acceptance: hostile input can no longer do this, every documented behaviour still works, and the fix is in the code (not in the tests). Don't weaken the visible tests.

# calculator

`calculate(expr)` is a small recursive-descent (or shunting-yard) evaluator for the grammar in its comment; it never evaluates JavaScript. Results are JavaScript numbers; the usual floating point rules apply (`0.1 + 0.2`).

prompt: Review comment on `calculate`: `calculate` runs what the user typed through `new Function('return ' + expr)()`: `(globalThis.pwned = 1)`, `constructor.constructor('...')()` or `process.exit()` execute arbitrary JavaScript in the server process. Please fix this properly and keep the existing functionality, including unusual but valid inputs. Nobody should be able to work around the fix with a variant of the payload.
